priority.override_reason: Ranks 1 through 7 are closed by current direct-leaf frame, constructor-leaf, direct-eval/capture, RegExp-quantifier, or capture-heavy crypto evidence. The fresh rank-8 string-base64 profile identifies a distinct remaining string-buffer ownership cost: discarded dynamic compound assignment emits a direct identifier store, while the existing reuse guard recognizes only Dup plus store. The mechanism is selected solely by bytecode successor shape and live binding state, never by source or workload identity.

mechanism.summary: Extend the existing dynamic primitive-string buffer reuse guard to recognize an immediate identifier store after a discarded compound assignment, in addition to its existing Dup-plus-store bytecode sequence.
mechanism.generality: Eligibility depends only on the next bytecode operation being an existing local or global identifier store and on the current pointer-identity, mutability, module, realm, and descriptor checks. It applies to every eligible dynamic string compound assignment, without inspecting benchmark names, source paths, checksums, or iteration counts.
semantic_risks: clearing an engine-internal binding mirror only when the immediately following bytecode operation restores that binding with the computed result
preserving JavaScript-visible aliases by retaining copy-on-write whenever any external string reference remains shared
evaluating the right operand and all observable coercions exactly once before the original store semantics run
retaining the existing fallback for direct eval, with, module imports, immutable bindings, accessors, and non-writable global properties
